issues.issue: The purpose clause defines "the Business" only as "Spanish language and bilingual print and media business," a phrase with no product, geographic or market boundary. Because that defined term drives the exclusivity in the LSB non-compete (c017) and the joint-pursuit promise (c011), its outer limit is left to argument.

Giving DMSA two of three board seats vests it with complete control of management, which sits uneasily with c004's allocation to LSB of day-to-day operations, hiring and joint development of long-term strategy. A court would have to decide which management power controls when the board and the Publisher disagree.

"Publisher" is a bare title: the provision fixes no term, no authority and no employment relationship, and the word is not defined anywhere in the agreement. Whether it creates a protected position (or any position at all) that DMSA could not remove is left open.

The grant to LSB of authority to manage day-to-day operations and to recruit and hire employees and contractors cannot be squared with c006, which subjects all expenditures to DMSA's concurrence, or with c020's budget restriction. A court would have to decide whether LSB could hire anyone at all without DMSA's assent.

"Will not contribute any cash to initiate the LLC" is limited by the word "initiate" and says nothing about later cash calls or about what LSB does give for her 49%. The temporal boundary of the acknowledgment, and whether services are her consideration, are both left unstated.

Requiring DMSA's concurrence for "all expenditures" cannot be squared with c020, which permits members to incur costs so long as they accord with the approved budget, nor with c004's grant of day-to-day management to LSB. Whether budgeted spending still needs item-by-item DMSA assent is unresolved.

DMSA's funding obligation is measured only by "an amount that DMSA deems appropriate," setting no floor and arguably making the promise illusory, while the parenthetical lets internal labor and overhead of DMSA staff count as contributed capital. Both the amount owed and what qualifies as "initial capital" are left to DMSA's say-so.

The clause is grammatically broken — "requiring approval by the Board of Directors issuing any additional membership interests" omits the connective, so it is unclear whether the Board must approve issuances or is itself the issuer. It also only promises a future agreement, leaving the right of first refusal's terms unspecified.

Pro rata distribution of all profits the board decides to distribute cannot be squared with c019, which routes amounts paid by clients first to out-of-pocket costs and then entirely to DMSA to repay its initial capital before anything is shared by interest. Which of the two governs a given dollar of profit is left unresolved.

The mandatory annual tax distribution conflicts with c019, which places the same tax payment third in a waterfall behind full repayment of DMSA's initial capital, and with c009's board discretion over distributions. A court would have to decide whether the tax distribution is owed even when the waterfall never reaches step three.

The promise that the parties "shall through the LLC jointly pursue the Business" cannot be squared with c013 and c014, which free DMSA and its principals of any duty to bring business to the LLC and let them keep and originate competing media and advertising clients for themselves. Whether c011 imposes any enforceable duty on DMSA at all is the question.

The acknowledgment that DMSA's principals may hold interests "whether similar to the LLC's Business or not" contradicts the joint-pursuit obligation in c011 and the exclusivity imposed on LSB in c017. The instrument does not say how far this carve-out cuts into the venture's own field.

The disclaimer of any obligation to originate or assign business for the LLC cannot be squared with c015, in which DMSA agrees to use diligent efforts to direct appropriate business to the Company. A court would have to decide whether c015 adds a duty or is wholly negated by this sentence.

DMSA's right to retain existing and originate new media opportunities, advertising contracts and clients "for its own benefit" cannot be squared with c011's joint pursuit of the Business or with c015's diligent-efforts commitment. Which business belongs to the LLC and which to DMSA is left for construction.

DMSA agrees only that it "intends to use diligent efforts" to direct "appropriate business" to the Company — a statement of present intention rather than a promise, with no standard for what business is "appropriate." Prefaced by "without diminishing DMSA's rights under the foregoing language," it may impose no enforceable duty at all.

"Diligent efforts" is undefined and the clause supplies no benchmark — no quota, time period or measure — by which LSB's origination efforts could be tested. The asymmetry with c015's weaker "intends to use diligent efforts" sharpens the question of what standard binds her.

"Such services" has no clear antecedent — it may mean only originating media and advertising contracts and clients, or all services relating to the Business — and the restraint carries no geographic or temporal limit and turns on the undefined phrase "the Business." "LSB nor its principals" is also incoherent as applied to an individual.

"Dialogo" is ambiguous: c001 names the new LLC itself Dialogo, so the sentence either says the LLC will rely on its own staff or refers to LSB's pre-existing Dialogo publication. "Initially" also fixes no period and the sentence states no terms, cost or duration for the staffing arrangement.

The waterfall's second priority — repaying DMSA "the initial capital to launch the LLC" — is measured by c007, where that capital is whatever amount DMSA "deems appropriate" and includes DMSA's own staff labor and overhead. Read together, the two provisions may prevent any dollar from ever reaching the third and fourth priorities, contradicting c010's mandatory annual tax distribution.

"Any out of pocket costs" is unattributed: the clause does not say whose costs, incurred by whom, or whether board or budget approval is a precondition to reimbursement. The first priority therefore has no ascertainable boundary.

The restriction turns on "the approved budget," but no provision of this Agreement creates a budget, says who prepares or approves it, or provides for what happens before one exists. Read against c006's requirement of DMSA concurrence for all expenditures, the two spending controls cannot both be the operative rule.

The sentence is garbled to the point of unintelligibility — apparently addressing borrowing by the Board "if approved by" some unidentified body — so its terms cannot be determined from the writing. Whether the LLC may borrow, and whose approval is required, is unascertainable on the face of the provision.

The confidentiality undertaking covers all "efforts and actions" taken for the LLC in connection with the Business, with no duration, no exception for publicly available or independently developed information, and no definition of what must be kept confidential. Its breadth cannot be reconciled with the narrower, defined category of Proprietary Information in c024.

Disclosure is permitted with "the prior written consent of the LLC," but the provision does not say who may give that consent — the Board, the members, or an officer — and no other provision supplies the mechanism. The covenant also has no stated term or exceptions.

The definition is a closed enumeration with no residual catch-all, so items not listed fall outside it (expressio unius), while the last item — "client provided information, documents and data" — is unbounded and swallows the specifics. What is and is not Proprietary Information is therefore contestable.

This provision contemplates a later operating agreement of the LLC, and the executed Operating Agreement and Members Agreement contains an integration clause (Section 17.8) superseding all prior agreements on the same subject. Whether the Venture Agreement survives the documents it calls for is squarely presented.

The clause requires the further documents to be consistent with this Agreement and to contain "standard terms and conditions," a phrase with no referent or source standard. It is an agreement to agree whose content cannot be fixed from the writing.
